entities.summary:
Robert Barnes (c. 1520–1540) was an English reformer and martyr.

As a prominent figure in the Protestant movement during the English Reformation, Barnes played a key role in shaping the theological landscape of the era.

During his lifetime, Barnes worked closely with other Reformers such as Martin Bucer and Peter Martyr, who were instrumental in shaping the Church of England's liturgy and doctrine.

Barnes' own contributions to the Protestant Reformation were significant, particularly in his role as a theologian and biblical interpreter.

One notable example of his influence can be seen in the 1549 Book of Common Prayer, which was compiled by the English Parliament with the help of Barnes and other Reformers.

Despite facing persecution from the Catholic Church and the English monarchy, Barnes remained committed to his faith until his death in 1540.

As a martyr for his beliefs, Barnes' legacy has endured as an important figure in the history of Protestantism.

"Theological orthodoxy is not merely a matter of doctrine but also of practical application," Barnes once said."
